claim: Let \(n\ge 2\), \(p<0\), and let \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\in S^{n-1}\) be linearly independent unit vectors. For positive masses \(\alpha_i^+,\alpha_i^-\), put \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^n(\alpha_i^+\delta_{u_i}+\alpha_i^-\delta_{-u_i})\), \(q=1-p\), let \(U\) have rows \(u_i^T\), and set \(d=|\det U|\), \(b_i=(\alpha_i^+)^{1/q}+(\alpha_i^-)^{1/q}\), \(B_i=b_i^{q/(q-1)}\), and \(\lambda=(d/\prod_j B_j)^{1/(n-p)}\). Then the unique convex body containing the origin in its interior with \(S_p(K,\cdot)=\mu\) is the parallelotope \(K=\{x:-a_i^-\le \langle x,u_i\rangle\le a_i^+,\ 1\le i\le n\}\), where \(w_i=\lambda B_i\) and \(a_i^\pm=w_i(\alpha_i^\pm)^{1/q}/b_i\). Thus the minimal spanning antipodal discrete problem has a closed-form inverse and is unique, including for unequal masses at opposite normals.
integrity: All formulas are derived explicitly from the facet support and \(L_p\) surface-area mass equations; external sources are used only for stated prior results and definitions.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to exactly \(n\) independent antipodal unit-normal pairs and \(p<0\); no uniqueness claim is made for larger discrete supports. Numerical replay is illustrative, not an infinite proof.
title: Closed-form uniqueness for the minimal antipodal \(L_p\) Minkowski problem
